rubric_notes: No evidence bundle. Family SCCS codes swapped (archaeal given as a.22.1.3, TAFs as a.22.1.2; actual 2.08: a.22.1.2 Archaeal, a.22.1.3 TAFs). States NF-Y and NC2 occupy 'a.22.1.4 and a later family' (a.22.1.4 is Bacterial histone-fold protein; NF-Y/NC2 are in a.22.1.3) = fabricated placement. Omits bacterial histone-fold family entirely (must_include). Places HU/IHF in class d (SCOPe: a.55.1). Superfamily-homology reasoning and function-transfer caveats are otherwise sound, but hard ceiling for materially wrong family classification caps bio at 2; fabricated release-specific classifications cap factual at 1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Biological framing (superfamily remote homology, family divergence, no substrate/pathway/mechanism/quaternary/template transfer) is sound, but family codes are wrong: MazG-like given as a.204.1.1, HisE-like as a.204.1.3, dUTPase as a.204.1.2 (actual: a.204.1.2, a.204.1.4, a.204.1.1), and this incorrect hierarchy is asserted as 'stable across SCOP 1.75 and SCOPe 2.0x releases (e.g., 2.07/2.08)' without evidence. No API evidence or sunids. Wrong family classification triggers the bio <= 2 ceiling.

Swaps the kinase families throughout (states c.55.1.4 = Hexokinase and c.55.1.3 = Glycerol kinase; SCOPe 2.08 has c.55.1.3 Hexokinase and c.55.1.4 Glycerol kinase), a material relationship-bearing misclassification that caps bio at 2; also asserts FGGY kinases such as xylulokinase sit in the glycerol kinase family, unsupported in 2.08. No evidence bundle. Otherwise the biological reasoning is excellent: superfamily-level remote homology with conserved motifs and closure mechanism, explicit unsafe transfers (substrate, regulation, catalytic competence, templates), and correct treatment of fold-level neighbours as not homologous. Factual support retains correct superfamily/fold/c.55.1.1 but the central family codes are wrong. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Meets all must_include: a.25.1.1/1.2/1.3 under a.25.1; superfamily read as probable common ancestry with chemistry divergence; explicit list of external evidence (HMM searches, superposition, metal/biochemical assays, family-specific residues). Avoids fold-level convergence and cross-family function transfer. Factual: no evidence bundle, no sunids or release citation; misplaces rubrerythrin N-terminal domain in a.25.1.2 (SCOPe 2.08 lists it under a.25.1.1); release-stability claim unsupported. Noncentral errors only. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Qualitative relationship (same superfamily b.6.1, different families) and refusal of copper/ET transfer are correct, but the family codes are wrong: ephrin given as b.6.1.4 (nitrosocyanin in SCOPe; correct b.6.1.5) and PAD4-N as b.6.1.5 (correct b.6.1.6); PAD4 middle and catalytic domains also misassigned (b.1.18, d.166.1 vs b.2.9.1, d.126.1.5). Wrong-family hard ceiling applied; no evidence bundle; unsupported release-stability claim. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Biological reasoning is complete: superfamily = probable common origin of a beta-grasp interaction scaffold, functions diverged; explicitly rejects transfer of conjugation, p97 binding and Ras binding across families, within-family caveats, fold-level MoaD/ThiS trap, external evidence list. Factual support weak: no evidence bundle, no release or sunids, identifiers self-described as 'approximate', and sibling families misassigned (APG12-like given as d.15.1.6 instead of d.15.1.7; 'DWNN' listed as d.15.1.7, not a d.15.1 family in 2.08). Central three family SCCS are correct.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. No evidence bundle. Misstates the families as c.23.1.2 (ODC wing) and c.23.1.3 'KaiA/RbsU domain' instead of c.23.1.4 and c.23.1.5, fills the wing family with eukaryotic ODC entries (7odc, 1d7k) although SCOPe c.23.1.4 holds only Lactobacillus ODC, and cites an 'additional C-terminal strand noted by SCOP for the ODC wing' that does not exist in the family annotations. Wrong family classification caps biological reasoning at 2; fabricated SCCS and annotation cap factual support at 1. Functional-limit reasoning (pseudo-receiver, non-catalytic wing, no fold-level homology) is otherwise sound.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. No evidence bundle; all identifiers from memory. Misstates the superfamily as b.84.4 (which is actually Ribosomal L27 protein-like) and never gives b.84.5 or any sunid; omits the b.84.4 L27 superfamily from the list of siblings the question asks about. Hard ceiling for a wrong superfamily applied to biological reasoning. The general fold-vs-superfamily reasoning and the agnostic (convergence vs ancient divergence) interpretation are sound, and cross-fold function transfer is correctly rejected, but the SCOPe-specific placement required by must_include is wrong/missing. Also describes the bulge as an insertion in the N-terminal barrel rather than inside the c.37.1.11 domain per SCOPe boundaries. Evidence is sparse with a major identifier error.

Correctly identifies fold f.21 with three separate superfamilies and f.21.3 as nitrate reductase gamma chain, but swaps the labels of f.21.1 (actually di-heme cytochromes) and f.21.2 (actually fumarate reductase subunits). Relationship structure and fold-vs-superfamily inference are right, convergence framed as plausible not proven, external evidence named. Release-inheritance claims about 2.07/2.08 are unsupported; no evidence bundle; misses the curators' 'possible link' caveat.

No evidence bundle; sccs codes c.2.1.1/c.2.1.8/c.2.1.9 under c.2.1 and the fold description are correct from general knowledge, and the Pfam/clan accessions cited are correct. Biological reasoning is strong: superfamily = probable common ancestry inferred from structure plus cofactor-binding mode, families = remote homologs with non-transferable function, fold similarity to other Rossmann-like folds is not homology, and limits on function, specificity residues and templates are explicit. Factual imprecision: states the c.2.1.1 SCOPe domain is often discontinuous because it is inserted within the GroES-like domain; the Rossmann domain is the continuous insert while the b.35 catalytic domain is the discontinuous one. No release or sunid support given. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Wrongly states the two domains are in different families and invents a '-1 suffix' SCOP convention for distinct families; both are in family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905). Omits the 'not a true family' annotation entirely and gives no sccs/sunids. Conclusion (no homology) and class k reasoning are sound, but wrong classification and ignored decisive annotation cap bio at 2; evidence sparse with major error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. No evidence bundle; answer from memory. Gets the general direction right (singleton fold in 1.69 -> same superfamily, separate family now) but misstates the current family as c.23.14.3 (actual c.23.14.2) and fabricates the 1.69 content of c.23.14 (claims ADP-ribosyl cyclase-like was c.23.14.2 in 1.69; in 1.69 the superfamily had a single family and ADP ribosyl cyclase-like is c.23.14.3 in 2.08). Never gives d1t1ja_ or d1t1ja1 identifiers or the 1.69 c.137 sccs. Invented active-site rationale details. Wrong family classification triggers bio ceiling <=2; fabricated release-specific classifications cap factual at 1. Caveats on function transfer are present and hedges that numbering should be verified.

Reasoning complete: tag in class l l.1.1.1 identified, d1a14h1 b.1.1.1 H:9-111 identified, homology rejection well argued with practical limits and fold-vs-homology caveats. Empty evidence bundle; classifications are correct but unverified, and release-history claims (split present 2.06-2.08, absent in 1.75) are plausible but unsupported. Factual 3 for lack of retrieved support rather than any demonstrated error.

Asserts 1.75 cut chain A into four domains and supplies a fabricated boundary table plus invented superfamily affiliations, violating the must_avoid criterion. Omits the real before/after comparison entirely: no d1acca_ / f.11.1.1, no 2.04 split, no A:14-225 / b.179.1.1 and A:226-735 / f.60.1.1. Treats the actual change as an unverified candidate edit, so the requested historical inference is not made; search advice is generic and detached from the real boundaries.

No evidence; from model memory (acknowledged). Wrong domain inventory: replaces the bromodomain (a.29.2.1) with a Jab1/MPN domain (c.97.3) not classified in this entry; no SIDs, boundaries, or d.394 identifier for the N-terminal domain. Mosaic and pseudoenzyme reasoning and function-transfer caveats are reasonable, but the misclassification of a relationship-bearing domain caps reasoning at 2.

The repeat-module reasoning and the function/template/representative limits are sound, but the answer omits the 're' heterogeneity annotation and the canonical representative repeat unit entirely, which caps biological reasoning. Supporting facts are substantially wrong: d2kq5a_ given as roughly 60-80 residues (51), d4cj9a_ asserted to be an AvrBs3-class array of about 17 repeats solved with DNA around 2013-2014 rather than apo BurrH from Burkholderia rhizoxinica, and family members characterized as orthologs of the same Xanthomonas protein despite the cross-genus member. Release history for a.298 is speculated. Hedging about confidence mitigates but does not repair the identifier errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Pretrained-only; no evidence bundle and explicitly cannot report the endpoint's actual latest periodic update, so the first must_include item is unmet. Stable 2.08 correct; citation guidance (stable 2.08 vs full dated periodic string, never 'current'/'latest') and periodic semantics (automated additions, identifiers preserved, hierarchy changes only in next stable release) are correct. Claim that periodic updates involve no manual curation is somewhat overstated but not a fabricated release fact.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Pretrained, no evidence. Wrongly states SCOPe treats fragments and full domain identically and carries entries forward unchanged: ignores the 'ms' fragment flag, the 'three-helical fragment' comment, and the move of d1dn1b_ to an automated match after 1dn1 obsolescence. Treats the three-helix Habc as the complete a.47 core so the fragment fold call was 'legitimately made', which conflicts with the four-helix fold definition and borders on fragment-only similarity as fold evidence (ceiling: decisive fragment annotation ignored). Munc18 misclassified as e.55.1.1 (actual e.25.1.1); SNARE complex given as h.1.1.1 (actual h.1.15.1). Family/superfamily/fold distinctions and function-transfer caveats are otherwise reasonable.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Good coverage of convergence vs divergence, level semantics, catalytic-triad parallel and evidence integration, but calls c.1.7/c.71/c.77/d.166 'clear-cut independent inventions' without the caveat that SCOPe placement does not prove independent origin. No evidence bundle. Minor classification error: NAD synthetase is in c.26.2 (adenine nucleotide alpha hydrolase-like), not c.26.1 (nucleotidylyl transferase); the claim that SCOPe release notes retain the c.2/c.3/c.31 separation is unsupported. Most other placements (c.25.1 with b.43.4, c.31.1, c.82, d.166.1, c.37) are correct.

Reverses the conclusion by asserting no change occurred and that both domains sat together in the Concanavalin A-like lectins/glucanases superfamily already in SCOP 1.75 and 2.04. That is wrong twice over: in 2.04 they were in different folds and superfamilies, b.23.2 versus b.18.1, and the shared current superfamily is Galactose-binding domain-like b.18.1, not Concanavalin A-like. The invented shared-superfamily history is a fabricated release-specific placement. Sound function-transfer caveats cannot offset a reversed central claim and absent supporting evidence.

No evidence retrieved. Misreads hf as a generic 'heterogeneous entry' weakening family-level evidence and speculates that 1ztr chain A has other regions in a different fold; misses that hf means the domain adopts a different fold from the exemplar. Asserts that the fold-level three-helix bundle 'is secure regardless of the flag', violating the must_avoid on assuming identical geometry. Treats the domains as possibly different proteins and recalls 1p7j as a DNA complex (wrong). Correct only in retaining superfamily-level homology and recommending hold-out of flagged entries.

Reasoning is thorough and correct: family-level homology unaffected, absent regions as missing data, local coverage-aware alignment, scores normalized to complete domain, fragment not a template, complete domain preferred over fragment even with better quality score, fragment-aware filtering before subsets, fragment retained but flagged, diversity from complete domains, no function transfer, release re-check. No evidence bundle: no sunids, boundaries, fr definition, or quality values for the recommended representative; vague on where the annotation is recorded. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct recommendation conditioned on meeting the fold criterion; family always implies superfamily-level ancestry claim (rejected), superfamily split asserts shared topology without common ancestry ('analogy or undetected homology', appropriately hedged), new fold = failure of core-topology criterion. Explicitly treats family/superfamily as homology hypotheses of different strength and fold/class as structural categories, revisable with new evidence; rejects fold-mate function transfer and homology-based modelling. Fold examples (c.1, d.58, b.40, b.1) and note on 2.07/2.08 manual curation are accurate; no API claims made. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Good discussion of superfamily homology, conserved catalytic motifs, non-transferable substrate/regulation and evidence needs, but misstates APH family as d.144.1.1 (actual d.144.1.6) and never identifies the PI3K family (d.144.1.4), so the must-include family set is incomplete and partly wrong. Hedged 'should be verified' but wrong family classification still triggers bio <= 2 ceiling. No evidence bundle; superfamily/fold/d.144.1.7 and PI3K accessory folds correct.
